description:
FILED s464aw (found by a #972 review probe; PRE-EXISTING -- verified identical
on an 80b715c worktree, so #972 did not cause or change it).

    my $h = {}; my $ar = []; my $bh = bless {}, 'C'; my $ba = bless [], 'C';
    join(",", $h)    perl HASH(0x...)     PCL  ""   <- EMPTY
    join(",", $ar)   perl ARRAY(0x...)    PCL  ""
    join(",", $bh)   perl C=HASH(0x...)   PCL  ""
    join(",", $ba)   perl C=ARRAY(0x...)  PCL  ""
    join(",", \$x)   perl SCALAR(0x...)   PCL  SCALAR(0x...)   <- works

    join(",", $bh, $bh)   perl "C=HASH(0x1),C=HASH(0x1)"   PCL ""  (no separator)
    join(",", $bh, "z")   perl "C=HASH(0x1),z"             PCL ",z"

So `join' treats a hash-ref / array-ref ARGUMENT as a container to SPREAD --
the reference is flattened away and contributes nothing (an empty ref
contributes zero elements; a non-empty one would contribute its CONTENTS).
Scalar refs are unaffected, and `"$ref"' interpolation is correct, so the
stringification is fine: it is the argument flattening.

SILENT WRONG, and it hits overloaded objects hardest -- `join(",", $obj)' on
a class with a `""' handler yields "" where perl yields the handler's string,
so every `join'-based report over objects loses them.

SUSPECT (not yet confirmed -- the cheap discriminating measurement): `p-join'
runs its arguments through `p-flatten-args' (or an equivalent), which spreads
a bare vector/hash-table payload.  A BOX holding a vector is a REFERENCE and
must not flatten; only a RAW container argument may.  Check `p-join' against
`p-print' (which is correct here -- `print $a, $a' works) and route the one
that is wrong through the other's rule.

BAR: the eight rows above vs perl; the sweep; a guard in an existing Pl/t
file.
subject: join() FLATTENS a hash-ref or array-ref argument -- the reference vanishes
